newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India drifts ahead of confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India drifts ahead of confidence vote.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts ended mixed in thin trade on Friday amid continued political concerns ahead of a key confidence vote in parliament.
Traders and brokers said volumes were limited following cautious trade in India and amid uncertainty about direction.
"It hinges on the budget and there is some form of optimism about that," a broker said.
Indian political leaders agreed on Friday to hold a special session of parliament later in April to try to salvage the 1997/8 budget whatever happened in the confidence vote.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 15-party United Front coalition is expected to lose the confidence vote, but analysts were hopeful that a compromise candidate could replace him and avert mid-term polls.
State Bank of India slipped 17 cents to $19.75/20.75 and Indian Hotels made 37 cents to $23.25/24.25.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.10 points, or 0.14 percent, down at 73.81 points, with the premium over the local market at 18.84 percent from 19.69 percent on Thursday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index rose 35.36 points to 3,633.73.
Taiwanese GDRs rebounded following Thursday's losses, the Capel Taiwan GDR Index adding 3.48 points or 2.71 percent to 131.99, representing a discount to the local market of 3.52 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.51 points, or 0.82 percent, up at 63.12, a premium of 27.63 percent over the local market.
